item.title: Granite Timeseries Ensemble provides a zero‑training default forecast recipe
item.description:
Granite Timeseries Ensemble provides a zero‑training default forecast recipe

Granite Timeseries Ensemble (Granite TSFM) introduces a default, zero‑training forecast recipe that combines four pre‑trained models.

🔍 Overview

  • Pre‑trained time‑series models can forecast without training on your dataset, but you still have to choose one.
  • Granite Timeseries Ensemble reduces that choice to a sensible default.
  • The default recipe combines four pre‑trained Granite models with different architectures, each capturing trends, seasonality, and local variation in different ways.

🧩 How it works

  • Two main ensemble recipes are provided:
    • Probabilistic Ensemble (uniform probability pooling)
    • IQR Ensemble (weights based on forecast spread)
  • Both recipes work with each member’s quantile forecasts (default 0.1 – 0.9) and produce a median and quantile forecasts.
  • Probabilistic Ensemble gives each member equal influence, pools quantile forecasts in probability space, and extracts the requested quantiles. No fitting step and no weighting hyperparameters are required.
  • IQR Ensemble approximates each member’s inter‑quartile range from the nearest 25th and 75th percentiles, then weights members inversely to their interval width. Weights vary by sample, target, and horizon step; isotonic regression keeps combined quantiles from crossing. A temperature setting and optional cap let users move weights toward uniform or limit any single member’s influence.

⚙️ Key details

  • Each member returns:
    • result.prediction_outputs – the point forecast.
    • result.quantile_outputs – quantile predictions ranging from 0.1 to 0.9.
  • The 0.1 and 0.9 quantiles define a central forecast interval with nominal 80 % coverage.
  • No retraining and no fitted ensemble weights; simple equal‑weight combinations have historically performed well in point forecasting.
  • The ensemble recipe stores the configuration rather than merged model weights; member checkpoints are downloaded at runtime, so allow extra time for the first run.
  • The recipe and its default Granite members are permissively licensed.
  • Both recipes were evaluated on 97 GIFT‑Eval dataset configurations (see the model card for full details, member checkpoints, evaluation, and limitations).

🚀 Availability

  • Install the package with: 
    1

    pip install "granite-tsfm>=0.3.11"
  • Load the recommended four‑model recipe directly from Hugging Face.
  • The model card provides the full configuration, member checkpoints, evaluation details, and known limitations.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a ready‑to‑use, zero‑training forecast solution for a wide range of series, from smooth industrial signals to noisy retail demand.
  • Reduces the risk of selecting a poor single model by combining diverse architectures; a 50‑year review of forecast combinations notes that such ensembles can lower error risk when members are high‑quality and diverse.
  • Enables applications to use the median as a central prediction and selected quantiles to express forecast uncertainty without any hyperparameter tuning.

#TimeSeries #Forecasting #Ensemble #Granite

Source: Ensemble forecasting with IBM Granite time-series models

item.title: IBM Updates Granite Speech Collection with New Multilingual and High-Speed Models
item.description:
IBM Updates Granite Speech Collection with New Multilingual and High-Speed Models

IBM has announced three updates to its Granite Speech collection: a new speech-language model called granite-speech-5.0-2b, and revised versions of granite-speech-5.0-470m-turboctc and granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus. These models are designed to cover enterprise speech requirements, including high-accuracy transcription, translation, and long-form multi-speaker analysis.

🔍 Overview

Model Primary Use Case Key Attributes
granite-speech-5.0-2b High-accuracy work 2B parameters, multilingual transcription and translation, keyword biasing
granite-speech-5.0-470m-turboctc Raw speed or edge use 470M parameters, 19,870 RTFx speed, native punctuation
granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus Meetings and multi-speaker calls Speaker attribution, tighter timestamps, 24% lower long-form WER

⚙️ Key details

granite-speech-5.0-2b

This model is the successor to granite-speech-4.1-2b and maintains the same parameter count. It was trained on 390,000 hours of public audio alongside synthetic data for Japanese ASR, translation, and keyword biasing.

  • Multilingual Capabilities: Transcribes English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese. Translates to and from English for those languages, plus English to Italian and Mandarin.
  • Advanced Prompting: Supports Language ID prompting and allows users to request formatted output; capitalization F1 ranges from 89.7 to 99.5 across test sets.
  • Accuracy: Features improved handling of noise, reverberation, and distant-microphone speech.
  • Keyword Biasing: Supports lists of up to 2,000 terms to bias transcription toward product names and acronyms.

granite-speech-5.0-470m-turboctc

Formerly an English-only model, this 470M-parameter encoder is now optimized for speed and multilingual use.

  • Multilingual Expansion: Now supports English, Japanese, Spanish, German, French, Italian, and Portuguese.
  • Performance Gains: The model is approximately 1.6x faster than its launch version, reaching 19,870 RTFx on the Open ASR Leaderboard by reusing a compiled Conformer block graph.
  • Edge Readiness: Includes native punctuation and capitalization, and supports browser-based streaming via WebGPU.

granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus

This is a drop-in replacement for the original 4.1-2b model, utilizing the same architecture, API, and prompt format with improved weights for long-form enterprise recordings.

  • Speaker Attribution: The word diarization error rate (WDER) and speaker-attributed WER (cpWER) both decreased by 7%.
  • Timing Precision: The average timestamp shift (AAS) has been cut by more than half, improving captions and search.
  • Long-Speech Performance: WER on long-form test sets decreased by 24%, while keyword biasing errors fell 45% when using 20-term lists.

🚀 Availability

The models are released under the Apache 2.0 license and include support for:

  • Transformers and vLLM
  • llama.cpp
  • mlx-audio for Apple Silicon

#IBM #Granite #SpeechRecognition #MachineLearning #OpenSource

Source: Granite Speech 5.0: Transcribe, Translate, and Attribute more Accurately and Faster
